methodological_rigor.justification: This retrospective single-center case series (n=60) from MD Anderson (2016–2024) represents one of the largest published cohorts of IVC leiomyosarcoma with systematic vascular management comparisons. Propensity score-weighted multivariate logistic regression is used to address confounding in the three-group comparison (IVC ligation n=10, IVC replacement n=36, patch angioplasty n=14), which is an appropriate method given the non-randomized design and small sample. Key limitations include: small total sample with very small subgroups (especially IVC ligation, n=10); single-center retrospective design with historical confounding (technique selection evolved over time); heterogeneous outcomes bundled into a composite 'major adverse events' endpoint; and the renal vein involvement subgroup (n=22) is too small for meaningful subgroup analysis. The chi-square comparison of adverse events without adjustment (p=0.225) and the PSM-adjusted results (p<0.001) show apparent discordance that is not fully explained in the text, raising concerns about small-sample instability.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This retrospective case series (LoE 4) addresses a clinically important but extremely rare indication — vascular management in IVC leiomyosarcoma resection — for which no randomized evidence exists and prior published series are largely single-digit case reports or very small series. The finding that IVC ligation is associated with higher adverse events compared to IVC replacement or patch angioplasty (on PSM-adjusted analysis) has direct surgical planning implications, particularly the observation that no patients required chronic hemodialysis after renal vein involvement. However, the evidence base is inherently limited by the rarity of the condition, the small sample, and the single-institution experience at a high-volume cancer center — limiting generalizability to lower-volume centers.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript follows general STROBE conventions for retrospective cohort studies: study design, eligibility criteria, exposure classification (vascular management approach), outcome definitions (major adverse events: bleeding, thromboembolism, reintervention), and statistical methods are described. Patient selection flowchart is absent. The composite adverse event endpoint components are defined but the individual component rates are not fully decomposed in the results. The discrepancy between unadjusted chi-square (p=0.225) and PSM-adjusted (p<0.001) results deserves more explicit explanation in the methods. Data are not publicly deposited. Operative and perioperative details are sufficient for clinical replication of the main approach comparisons.

novelty_literature.justification: This is one of the largest single-institution series specifically examining vascular management strategies in IVC leiomyosarcoma resection, extending prior work that consisted predominantly of small case series and technical reports. The systematic comparison of three management approaches (ligation, replacement, patch angioplasty) with propensity-adjusted outcomes, and the focused subgroup analysis of renal vein involvement, provide more structured comparative data than prior publications. However, the core message — that IVC reconstruction may be preferable to ligation in selected patients — has been suggested in prior case series; the incremental contribution is primarily the larger sample and statistical adjustment rather than a conceptually novel finding.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with clear sections for patient selection, vascular management approaches, and surgical outcomes. The rationale for comparing the three management strategies is clearly articulated, and the discussion appropriately contextualizes the findings within the extremely limited existing literature. The acknowledgment of selection bias and the evolution of technique over time as limitations is transparent. Minor issues include the unexplained discrepancy between unadjusted and PSM-adjusted statistical results, which may confuse readers without additional explanation, and some repetition between the results and discussion sections.

key_strengths: One of the largest published single-institution series of IVC leiomyosarcoma vascular management, providing comparative data across three surgical approaches (ligation, replacement, patch angioplasty) that are unavailable from prior small case reports
Propensity score-weighted analysis to address confounding in a non-randomized rare-disease cohort — a methodologically appropriate approach given the impossibility of randomization in this setting

Clinically important finding that no patient in the renal vein involvement subgroup required chronic hemodialysis, providing reassurance about renal outcomes that directly informs preoperative counseling
key_concerns: Very small subgroup sizes (especially IVC ligation n=10) severely limit statistical power; the PSM-adjusted analysis may be unstable with these sample sizes and the unexplained discordance with unadjusted results (p=0.225 vs. p<0.001) requires explicit clarification

Single-center retrospective design with technique selection evolving over the study period introduces substantial historical confounding that PSM cannot fully resolve — more recent patients predominantly received IVC replacement, potentially conflating technique preference with era effects

Composite adverse event endpoint bundles clinically distinct outcomes (bleeding, thromboembolism, reintervention) of varying severity that may have different relationships with vascular management approach
Generalizability is limited to high-volume sarcoma centers; outcomes at institutions without dedicated vascular surgery support may differ substantially from this MD Anderson experience
chief_reviewer.rationale: This retrospective case series represents the current best available evidence for a rare and challenging surgical problem, and the propensity-adjusted comparative data are a genuine contribution to the limited literature on IVC leiomyosarcoma management. The small sample, historical confounding, and unexplained statistical discordance are meaningful limitations; minor revisions to clarify the PSM methodology and reconcile the unadjusted vs. adjusted results are warranted before Tier 3 acceptance.
